set.body:
DOCUMENTED PROMISE NOT KEPT. introduction.Rmd:319-321 states:

  'Compile the reusable scientific plan before choosing whether to query or materialize it.
   Plan construction validates sources, axes, the frame, pairing, and COMPUTE POLICY without
   reading a neural block'

Measured: an unsatisfiable workspace budget passes plan construction and fails later.

  plan_geometry(rel, at, over, compute = compute_policy(workspace_bytes = 1))
    -> plan built successfully

  geometry(that_plan)
    -> The conservative memory plan requires 111360 bytes, exceeding the 1-byte budget.

So the compute policy is validated at MATERIALIZATION, not at plan construction. The check itself is correct and does precede any block reading - the figure is a shape-derived estimate, not a measurement - so no data is touched and no memory is wasted. Nothing is broken. But the sentence promises the check happens one step earlier than it does.

WHY IT IS WORTH A BEAD DESPITE BEING SMALL. The entire argument for the plan object is that it lets a user find out early whether a scientific request is well formed, before committing to expensive work. bd-01KZYAV8X93BX4VC13Z8PK8XRH and the API discussion both lean on that property. A budget that cannot possibly be satisfied is exactly the class of error a user would most want caught at plan time, and it is the one named in the sentence that is not caught there.

FIX, either direction and both are cheap:
  1. move the conservative workspace estimate into plan_geometry() so the promise holds, or
  2. amend the sentence to say plan construction validates sources, axes, frame and pairing,
     and that the workspace budget is checked when the plan is executed

I lean to 1, because the estimate is derived from shapes the plan already holds, so it should cost nothing to compute there.

EVERYTHING ELSE IN THIS AREA IS SOUND, and I want that recorded alongside:

  budget enforced correctly     1e9 and 1e6 allowed, 1e4 / 1e3 / 1 blocked, with the exact
                                requirement named in bytes
  query-first is genuinely
  cheaper                       materialized needs 111360 bytes; the same request query-first
                                needs 59300 - a 47 percent reduction, which is quantitative
                                confirmation of the design claim rather than an assertion
  nonsense budgets refused      -1, 0, NA and Inf all rejected with
                                'workspace_bytes must be NULL or one positive finite number'
  workers > 1 refused           'workers > 1 is not implemented in effectagram 0.1;
                                workers must be 1' - one of the five genuinely good messages

The query-first figure is worth carrying into the API discussion on bd-01KZYAV8X93BX4VC13Z8PK8XRH: the wrapper that routes query-first is not merely semantically safe, it needs materially less workspace, which strengthens the case for it independently of ergonomics.
set.title: Plan construction is documented to validate the compute policy, but an unsatisfiable budget passes it
